editorial_policy: Accessible textual adaptation faithful to the original themes, not an exact graphical copy of the slides; unverified pedagogical quotations are identified as paraphrases

slides.title: Artificial intelligence and applied teaching
slides.lead: Turn AI from an automatic content generator into a tool for educational design
points: The teacher sets and guides the learning objective
The system can draft materials, not certify that learning occurred
slides.takeaway: Technology serves pedagogy, not the other way around

slides.title: The myth of instant productivity
slides.lead: The promise: 30 perfect slides in 20 seconds
points: Quantity does not measure lesson quality
Time saved during generation must be compared with the time required for verification
Ask what evidence would show that students genuinely understood
slides.takeaway: What evidence shows that the lesson actually works?

slides.title: The danger of a well-designed mistake
slides.lead: One slide places the first Industrial Revolution in 1925
points: The example deliberately contains a historical anachronism
Polished design can make a false claim seem credible
The model does not automatically understand the class context
slides.takeaway: AI produces drafts; the teacher remains responsible for checking sources

slides.title: From software to method
slides.lead: The MANZO AI method as an organisational proposal
points: 1 · Listen — what problem are we addressing?
2 · Classify — which class and objective?
3 · Risks — errors, privacy, access barriers?
4 · Targeted questions — what is missing?
5 · Design — which activity or prompt?
6 · Verify — content and learning?
7 · Deliver — what do we offer, and within which limits?
slides.takeaway: This method is an adaptable practical proposal, not a scientifically validated standard

slides.title: A prompt is not a magic formula
slides.lead: From “create a beautiful lesson” to verifiable teaching instructions
points: AI should not decide the learners' age, prerequisites and sources on its own
A better request makes priorities clear without necessarily being very long
The teacher retains control over educational variables
slides.takeaway: A good prompt starts with instructional design

slides.title: Six elements of an educational prompt
slides.lead: A guide to producing drafts that can be checked
points: Objective — what will learners be able to do?
Context — subject, level, duration, prerequisites
Permitted data — sources and materials that may be used
Constraints — safety, accessibility, accuracy
Output — the required form of the response
Verification — checks, limitations and claims that cannot be inferred
slides.takeaway: An effective prompt is a brief whose output can be verified

slides.title: Objective and context
slides.lead: Who is learning, and what should we be able to observe?
points: Objective: distinguish fact and interpretation in a short document
Context: second-year upper-secondary class, 15 minutes, pair work, clear language
Observable performance: justify a distinction, not merely recall a definition
slides.takeaway: First decide what learning should look like, then choose the material

slides.title: Permitted data and boundaries
slides.lead: Protect students and avoid inventing what we do not know
points: Use sources already checked or examples clearly marked as fictional
Do not upload real names, grades, photographs or personal information to unauthorised tools
Do not add nonexistent statistics or historical citations
Plan legible materials and accessible alternatives
slides.takeaway: Data minimisation is a design choice; it does not by itself certify GDPR compliance

slides.title: Output and verification
slides.lead: Define both the format and the evidence of learning
points: One guiding question
Three steps with suggested timings
Two questions for pair work
An exit ticket that checks understanding
A list of what cannot be inferred from the documents

slides.title: From a generic to a targeted request
slides.lead: “Create a lesson on migration” is not enough
points: A generic request leaves purpose, sources, audience and criteria unspecified
A targeted request describes the six prompt elements
The targeted draft is easier to read, correct and adapt
No prompt automatically guarantees truth or safety
slides.takeaway: The teacher evaluates the work rather than simply accepting it

slides.title: Authentic assessment beyond AI detectors
slides.lead: Do not chase a percentage: ask learners to demonstrate their reasoning
points: Selection and verification of sources
Argumentation and defence of claims
Reflection on revisions and next steps
A detector alone cannot conclusively establish the author of a text
slides.takeaway: Assess competence; do not infer misconduct from the appearance of an assignment

slides.title: The pedagogical perspective
slides.lead: A lived problem can generate hypotheses, inquiry and revision
points: A meaningful problem encourages questions
Questions guide testable hypotheses
Evidence can confirm, change or challenge an initial view
The original slide's reference to Dewey is a pedagogical paraphrase, not a verified verbatim quotation
slides.takeaway: Education as reflective inquiry, not entertainment

slides.title: The question always comes first
slides.lead: The teacher's question comes before the machine's response
points: The objective and context guide the activity
A system cannot replace educational judgment
Choosing not to use AI can be a well-reasoned educational decision
slides.takeaway: One good question is worth more than thirty slides

slides.title: The teacher's professional toolkit
points: Italy's Ministry of Education and Merit, 2025 — guidance on AI in schools
European Commission, 2026 — ethical guidance
UNESCO, 2024 — AI competencies for teachers
CAST UDL 3.0 — inclusion and accessibility
Always check whether a source is up to date and applicable
slides.takeaway: Professional practice rests on accountability, not a race to adopt tools

slides.title: One question to carry forward
slides.lead: If artificial intelligence suddenly stopped working tomorrow, would what you learned today still make you a better teacher?
points: Keep the useful questions
Keep the capacity to verify
Keep the ability to design learning
Experiment intentionally, without delegating your judgment
slides.takeaway: Start with the needs of the class
